scope: Source-backed research on making MiniMax H3/FastH3 video content follow requirements; no model download, GPU run, private-media copy, or product/skill edit.

answer.mode_boundary: FastH3 Preview v1 4-step and FastH3 8-Step V2 public cards are T2AV-only students. Native H3 Ref2VA uses a separate reference transformer. Feeding shared ComfyUI native reference conditioning into a FastH3 T2VA student is experimental_ref2va_ood and is not a reference-fidelity guarantee.
answer.prompt_contract: Choose the actual mode first. Ref2VA uses subject_definitions, summary, retention_analysis, detailed_description, overall_soundscape, non_diegetic_music. Base modes use the documented alignment line when applicable plus integrated_multimodal_description, overall_soundscape, non_diegetic_music. Stable reference labels and speaker IDs must match serialized inputs and actual vocal order.
answer.acceptance_contract: Inspect original-size frames and the supplied references for identity, hair, costume, prop count/orientation/geometry, action causality, scene/shot continuity, and audio/dialogue; separately verify decoded fps, frame count, duration, audio sample rate/channels, and subtitle/ASR timing. Successful decode is not content pass.

sources.title: MiniMax H3 h3-prompt-writing skill and base/ref guides
facts: Modes are T2VA, I2VA, FL2VA, L2VA, and Ref2VA.
Ref2VA sections are ordered subject_definitions, summary, retention_analysis, detailed_description, overall_soundscape, non_diegetic_music.
Reference labels keep their meaning across sections; a picture used only to define identity/costume is cited inside a Subject, while a concrete keyframe can be a standalone Picture.
Base prompts place visuals, actions, speakers, dialogue, and diegetic audio on the timeline; stable S IDs follow actual vocal order; dialogue stays verbatim in <d>; soundscape excludes dialogue.
Later shots use strictly increasing cut times within the requested duration; the guide recommends concrete visual/audio detail over abstract adjectives.

sources.title: MiniMax H3 model card
facts: FL2VA supports zero, one, or two input images for T2V, first/last-frame, or first-and-last-frame use.
Ref2VA supports at most 9 images, 3 video clips (each 2-15 seconds, total 15 seconds), 3 audio clips (same duration limits), and 12 mixed files.
FL2VA and Ref2VA are separate task-specific BF16 checkpoints; the README lists reproducible local 768p T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA cases.

sources.title: ComfyUI native MiniMax H3 node and official R2V guide
facts: Reference presentation order is images, then videos (paired soundtrack label before its video), then standalone audio; ordinals are 1-based per type.

The node exposes up to 9 images, 3 videos, 3 video soundtracks, and 3 standalone audio clips. ref_image_size=match scales down to generation area; max uses up to a 2048px short edge and can be slower; references are never upscaled.
A video reference is sampled for Qwen at 2 fps with timestamps, while the VAE block keeps its 24-fps frames. A video needs at least 5 frames and is cropped to the 17k+5 grid.

The official R2V guide says to assign each reference a job (identity, style, motion, camera, voice), and says R2V uses ref2va weights distinct from fl2va; these are input guidance/weight boundaries, not output guarantees.

sources.title: FastVideo FastH3 4-step and 8-Step V2 model cards
facts: 4-step Preview is a four-forward, step-1300, data-free DMD2/VSA-H3 T2AV checkpoint with 90% sparsity and 64-token tiles; its card says difficult motion, fine detail, and some audio may remain below base H3.
8-Step V2 is a different eight-forward, step-1300 DMD2/VSA-H3 T2AV checkpoint with 80% sparsity and 64-token tiles; its card also says FL2VA and Ref2VA were not distilled.
The cards support a matched schedule/seed/prompt comparison, but do not establish that 4 steps always fail or 8 steps always repair fidelity.

sources.title: FastVideo distilled checkpoint schedules
facts: FastH3 OmniRef PDD-8 is a separate Ref2VA transformer_ref student with 32 PDD heads sampled in eight blocks; references must be ordered and at least one image or video is required.
Its contract uses Ref2VA shifts 12/3, VSA reference policy p2_multi_region, and 128-token tiles.

The 128-token PDD reference path runs only on sm100a/sm103a block-sparse kernels and has no Triton fallback; the documented GB200 example peaks near 103 GiB for a 480x832 124-frame request. This is not an L4 suitability claim.

sources.title: Local final-03 known limitations
facts: A nine-segment Original50 BF16 Ref2VA assembly passed media decode/format checks but retained only approximate identity; face/hair, collar/belt/skirt details, arrow feather/shaft geometry/direction, and moon-scene details varied across segments.
The README explicitly says the run was not a fair 8-versus-50 comparison and does not claim full identity consistency; audio was not manually heard in that environment.

operational_matrix.action: Select actual T2VA/FL2VA/Ref2VA mode; keep official fields/labels/order; put dialogue in timed detailed description; use stable S IDs; store final serialized prompt.
operational_matrix.boundary: Input conformance only; no output fidelity guarantee.
operational_matrix.acceptance: Parse prompt, verify every label maps to an actual ordered input, inspect shot times against duration, and check dialogue timing.

operational_matrix.action: Record source path/hash, pixel crop, role, node socket order, ref_image_size, and VAE connections; compare match vs max only with the same seed/prompt.
operational_matrix.boundary: Comfy native Ref2VA behavior; FastH3 T2VA plus ref conditioning is OOD. max is a speed/conditioning tradeoff, not a face lock.
operational_matrix.acceptance: Inspect reference manifest and original-size output face/hair/costume at close, speech, turn, and maximum-motion frames.

operational_matrix.action: Define one Subject for the person; bind original photo to identity and costume image/text to clothing; if same person has multiple refs say so explicitly.
operational_matrix.boundary: Subject/retention language is model intent; multiple images are not proven better and exact-face words are not hard constraints.
operational_matrix.acceptance: Compare face shape/eyes/nose/mouth/hair/age impression and full-body garment separately against original refs.

operational_matrix.action: Use a positive physical chain with one actor/one prop and explicit count, hand, direction, release, trajectory, and impact; isolate in a short shot before mixing with identity/camera moves.
operational_matrix.boundary: Operational hypothesis derived from prompt semantics and local failures; no source proves wording guarantees geometry.
operational_matrix.acceptance: Dense frame sampling checks arrow count, shaft/feather continuity, aim direction, causal release, and hit location.

operational_matrix.action: Use an independent empty-scene prompt that names visible lunar surface, Earth/sky placement, camera direction, lighting, and temporal change; keep character descriptions out of that shot.
operational_matrix.boundary: A clean empty shot does not prove other shots or cross-segment background continuity.
operational_matrix.acceptance: Check first/middle/last and dense samples for unwanted people, extra celestial objects, scene swaps, and landmarks.

operational_matrix.action: Use exact original dialogue inside <d>; assign S IDs by actual vocal event; keep soundscape free of dialogue; preserve audio and subtitle time bases.
operational_matrix.boundary: ASR can hallucinate words or miss speech; no audio input support in the local final-03 run means no manual-hearing claim there.
operational_matrix.acceptance: Cross-check decoded audio, waveform/duration, ASR word times, subtitle times, and manual listening when available.

operational_matrix.action: Use each checkpoint's own trained ladder/shifts/backend; compare same prompt, refs, crop, seed, dimensions, duration, and event frames.
operational_matrix.boundary: 4 vs 8 and 50 comparisons are only case-specific unless all other variables match; schedule endpoint conventions differ by runtime.
operational_matrix.acceptance: Score identity, action causality, geometry, scene, audio, and cross-segment continuity separately; do not replace content QA with speed or successful decode.

unverified_hypotheses: Explicit role assignment, affirmative physical descriptions, reduced reference ambiguity, and separated character/action shots may improve this task, but no checked source quantifies or guarantees the effect.
A max-size or face-focused crop may preserve more identity information than match-size input, but the local references explicitly call this a design choice rather than an identity guarantee.
FastH3 T2VA plus shared native Ref2VA reference nodes may produce useful OOD behavior, but no source or local run establishes its reference fidelity.
not_supported_claims: A specific word guarantees an unchanged face or unwarped object.
More reference images always improve identity.
Four steps always produce bad quality, or eight steps always fix it.
An OmniRef PDD contract is an L4 recipe.
